# ethereum-optimism/ecosystem Monthly Report (April 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In April 2026, development activity focused heavily on hardening the reliability of the Optimism test suite and maintaining a modern dependency stack. Significant progress was made in resolving long-standing flaky tests and refining the `op-supernode` service level agreements. A major technical discussion also emerged regarding the `op-node` runtime configuration, specifically addressing how verifier nodes handle unsafe block signer address rotations to prevent stale signer windows.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Infrastructure & Dependency Management
The team executed a series of routine but essential dependency updates to ensure security and performance across the ecosystem's applications.
*   **Frontend & Tooling:** Updated `vite` from 4.5.14 to 6.4.2 ([#985](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/985)) and `fast-xml-parser` to 4.5.6 ([#990](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/990)).
*   **Backend Services:** A coordinated update of the `hono` web framework and `drizzle-orm` was completed across several packages, including `ponder-interop` ([#986](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/986), [#987](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/987), [#988](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/988), [#989](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/989)).

### Protocol & Node Refinement
*   **Supernode SLA:** The definition of the Superroot SLA within `op-supernode` was finalized, improving the consistency and behavior of Superroot objects ([#19180](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19180)).
*   **Runtime Config Reloads:** A draft PR ([#19982](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/19982)) was initiated to implement a reactive reload mechanism for `op-node`. This aims to solve the issue of gossip blocks failing signature verification when a signer address is rotated, potentially replacing the static 10-minute reload interval with a more responsive trigger.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Test Reliability:** Several flaky tests were successfully stabilized and closed, including `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` ([#19897](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19897)) and `TestExecutePayloadSuccess` ([#19898](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19898)).
*   **Acceptance Testing:** Acceptance tests for invalid executing messages were unskipped, signaling increased confidence in the interop message validation logic ([#19712](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19712)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Persistent Flakiness in Flashblocks:** The `TestFlashblocksTransfer` ([#19934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19934)) and `TestFlashblocksStream` ([#19883](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19883)) issues remain active. Logs indicate timing races where transaction block times exceed flashblock times, and instances where `op-node` fails to stop the sequencer due to context cancellations.
*   **L2 Chain Reorgs:** `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL` ([#19936](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19936)) continues to show "operation failed permanently" errors, suggesting the expected head is not matching the "unsafe" state after reorgs.
*   **Interoperability Testing:** Work is ongoing to migrate `op-e2e` interop action tests to the `op-acceptance-tests` suite to streamline CI and improve proof setup cleanup ([#18974](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/18974)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month was characterized by deep technical troubleshooting between core contributors. Notable collaboration occurred between `wwared` and `maurelian` regarding the debugging of flashblock timing issues, involving detailed analysis of CI run contexts and error logs. Discussions around `op-node` configuration ([#19981](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19981)) showed an active effort to balance protocol security with operational flexibility, weighing options like "grace periods" for old keys versus more frequent configuration polling.
